checks.label: Dirty Pipe (CVE-2022-0847) - Kernel 5.8-5.16.11
checks.command: uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[.-]' '{v=$1"."$2"."$3; if($1==5 && ($2>8 || ($2==8)) && (($2<16) || ($2==16 && $3+0<=11))) print "VULNERABLE kernel "v; else print "NOT_AFFECTED kernel "v}'
checks.description: CVE-2022-0847 (Dirty Pipe) allows unprivileged write to read-only files including SUID binaries, enabling local privilege escalation to root. Affects Linux 5.8 through 5.16.11/5.15.25/5.10.102.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to >= 5.16.12 or apply the specific backport patch. Verify Android Security Bulletin patch for March 2022.
checks.why: Dirty Pipe allows any process to overwrite arbitrary read-only file-backed page cache data, enabling root escalation via SUID binary overwrite.
checks.risk_if_fail: Any app or shell user can escalate to root by overwriting SUID binaries.

checks.label: Bad Binder (CVE-2019-2215) - Use-After-Free in Binder
checks.command: uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[.-]' '{maj=$1+0; min=$2+0; pat=$3+0; if(maj<4 || (maj==4 && min<14) || (maj==4 && min==14 && pat<150) || (maj==4 && min==19 && pat<57)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE"; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED"}'
checks.description: CVE-2019-2215 (Bad Binder) is a use-after-free in the Android Binder IPC driver exploitable for local privilege escalation. Actively exploited by Triada malware. Unpatched kernels < 4.14.150 / 4.19.57 are at risk.
checks.remediation: Apply Android Security Bulletin October 2019 patch or update kernel. Verify security patch level >= 2019-10-06.
checks.why: Bad Binder was exploited in-the-wild by Triada malware for kernel-level root escalation on millions of Android devices.
checks.risk_if_fail: Malicious app can escalate to kernel ring-0 privileges via Binder IPC race condition.

checks.label: Binder Out-of-Bounds (CVE-2020-0041)
checks.command: getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | awk -F'-' '{y=$1; m=$2; if(y<2020 || (y==2020 && m+0<3)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE SPL="y"-"m; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED SPL="y"-"m}'
checks.description: CVE-2020-0041 is an out-of-bounds write in Binder driver enabling local privilege escalation. Fixed in Android Security Bulletin March 2020 (2020-03-05 SPL).
checks.remediation: Update security patch level to >= 2020-03-05. Apply Android Security Bulletin March 2020 patches.
checks.why: Binder out-of-bounds write can corrupt kernel memory and escalate privileges from any app sandbox.
checks.risk_if_fail: Apps can escape sandbox and gain kernel privileges via crafted Binder transactions.

checks.label: epoll Use-After-Free (CVE-2021-1048)
checks.command: getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | awk -F'-' '{y=$1; m=$2; if(y<2021 || (y==2021 && m+0<11)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE SPL="y"-"m; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED SPL="y"-"m}'
checks.description: CVE-2021-1048 is a use-after-free in the Linux epoll subsystem allowing local privilege escalation. Fixed in Android Security Bulletin November 2021 (2021-11-06 SPL).
checks.remediation: Update security patch level to >= 2021-11-06. Apply Android Security Bulletin November 2021 patches.
checks.why: epoll use-after-free can be exploited by malicious apps for kernel privilege escalation.
checks.risk_if_fail: Malicious app can achieve kernel-level code execution via epoll file descriptor manipulation.

checks.label: MTK-su (MediaTek Privilege Escalation Tool)
checks.command: find /data/local/tmp /sdcard /system/xbin 2>/dev/null -name 'mtk-su' -o -name 'mtk_su' 2>/dev/null | head -5
checks.description: MTK-su is a MediaTek-specific privilege escalation tool exploiting a backdoor in MediaTek SoC drivers. Grants instant root on affected devices.
checks.remediation: Remove mtk-su binary immediately. Update to firmware with MediaTek security patches applied.
checks.why: MediaTek inadvertently left a debug backdoor in production SoC drivers allowing any app to gain root without exploit.
checks.risk_if_fail: Complete device compromise - any unprivileged process can gain root shell.

checks.label: MTK Engineering Mode (Debug Backdoor)
checks.command: getprop ro.mediatek.platform 2>/dev/null && ls /dev/mtk* 2>/dev/null | head -5
checks.description: MediaTek platform detected. Verify MTK engineering mode is disabled and check for mtk-su vulnerability (affected Helio P35/P60/G90 and others).
checks.remediation: Check if MTK engineering mode is disabled. Ensure MediaTek security patch applied (2020-04 or later for affected chipsets).

checks.label: MTK-su Exploit Entry Point (/proc/mtk_su)
checks.command: ls /proc/mtk_su 2>/dev/null
checks.description: /proc/mtk_su is the kernel interface exploited by MTK-su for instant root on MediaTek devices. Its presence confirms the device is vulnerable.
checks.remediation: Apply MediaTek security update. This proc entry should not exist in patched firmware.

checks.label: Stagefright Patch Level (CVE-2015-1538 family)
checks.command: getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | awk -F'-' '{y=$1; if(y<2016) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE - SPL before 2016"; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED SPL="$0}'
checks.description: Stagefright (CVE-2015-1538 family) was a critical Android mediaserver vulnerability. Devices with SPL before 2016 are at risk.
checks.remediation: Update to Android security patch level 2015-10-01 or later for Stagefright fixes.
checks.why: Stagefright allowed remote code execution via MMS without user interaction on billions of Android devices.

checks.label: Dirty COW (CVE-2016-5195) - Kernel < 4.8.3
checks.command: uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[.-]' '{maj=$1+0; min=$2+0; pat=$3+0; if(maj<4 || (maj==4 && min<8) || (maj==4 && min==8 && pat<3)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE"; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED"}'
checks.description: CVE-2016-5195 (Dirty COW) is a race condition in copy-on-write that allows unprivileged local privilege escalation. Affects Linux < 4.8.3.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to >= 4.8.3 or apply backport patch. Verify security patch level >= 2016-12-01.
checks.why: Dirty COW has been actively exploited in Android malware (ZNIU) for root escalation.

checks.label: Exynos Baseband Vulnerability Indicators (CVE-2023-24033)
checks.command: getprop ro.board.platform 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'exynos|s5e|samsung' && getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | awk -F'-' '{y=$1; m=$2; if(y<2023 || (y==2023 && m+0<3)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE to CVE-2023-24033"; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED"}'
checks.description: CVE-2023-24033: Exynos Shannon baseband modem zero-click RCE via SIP/VoLTE. Affects Exynos 850/980/1080/2100/2200/1280/1380/1330/W920/Modem 5123/5300. Patch in March 2023 SPL.
checks.remediation: Apply March 2023 Android Security Bulletin patch. Consider disabling VoLTE/WiFi Calling on affected Exynos devices until patched.

checks.label: Qualcomm msm_perf / perf Privilege Escalation (CVE-2019-10567)
checks.command: ls /dev/msm_perf 2>/dev/null || ls /dev/energy-awareness 2>/dev/null
checks.description: Qualcomm performance driver devices (/dev/msm_perf) have had privilege escalation vulnerabilities. Verify patches applied.
checks.remediation: Apply Qualcomm security updates and Android Security Bulletin patches for your chipset.

checks.label: Futex Privilege Escalation (CVE-2014-3153 / Towelroot)
checks.command: uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F'[.-]' '{maj=$1+0; min=$2+0; pat=$3+0; if(maj<3 || (maj==3 && min<14) || (maj==3 && min==14 && pat<5)) print "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE (Towelroot era kernel)"; else print "LIKELY_PATCHED"}'
checks.description: CVE-2014-3153 (Towelroot) is a futex requeue privilege escalation affecting kernels < 3.14.5. Historic but relevant for legacy devices.
checks.remediation: Update kernel. Legacy Android devices on very old kernels should be replaced.
checks.why: Towelroot was one of the first widely automated Android root exploits, affecting many legacy devices still in production.

checks.label: Vulnerable Kernel Modules Loaded
checks.command: cat /proc/modules 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'mali|pvrsrvkm|kgsl|msm_|exynos' | awk '{print $1}' | head -10
checks.description: GPU/SoC kernel modules loaded. Mali (CVE-2023-26083), PowerVR (various), Adreno (Qualcomm) drivers have had high-severity CVEs.
checks.remediation: Informational. Ensure vendor kernel patches for GPU drivers are applied via monthly security bulletins.

checks.label: Mali GPU Driver (CVE-2023-26083 / CVE-2022-46891)
checks.command: cat /proc/modules 2>/dev/null | grep mali | head -3
checks.description: Mali GPU driver loaded. CVE-2023-26083 (Mali memory disclosure) and CVE-2022-46891 (use-after-free) were actively exploited. Verify patch status.
checks.remediation: Apply Arm Mali GPU driver security updates. Check Android Security Bulletin for device-specific Mali patches.

checks.label: WebView Debugging Enabled (debug.webview)
checks.command: getprop debug.webview.debug 2>/dev/null; getprop persist.webview.debug 2>/dev/null
checks.description: When debug.webview.debug or the equivalent setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled is on, any chrome://inspect client can attach to in-app WebViews, expose the DOM, and run arbitrary JavaScript in the app's context. Should be off in production, especially for payment and IoT control UIs that use WebView.
checks.remediation: Disable WebView debugging in production builds. Remove WebView.setWebContentsDebuggingEnabled(true) from app code, and ensure debug.webview.debug is not set.

checks.label: Copy Fail (CVE-2026-31431) algif_aead page-cache write
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F"[.-]" "{printf \"%d.%d.%d\", \$1, \$2, \$3}"); ka=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f1); kb=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f2); kc=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f3); vuln=0; case "${ka}.${kb}" in 4.*) vuln=1 ;; 5.10) [ "$kc" -lt 254 ] && vuln=1 ;; 5.15) [ "$kc" -lt 204 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.1)  [ "$kc" -lt 170 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.6)  [ "$kc" -lt 137 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.12) [ "$kc" -lt 85 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.18) [ "$kc" -lt 22 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.19) [ "$kc" -lt 12 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 5.*|6.*) vuln=1 ;; esac; [ "$vuln" = "1" ] && echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v" || echo "LIKELY_PATCHED kernel $v"'
checks.description: Linux kernel crypto/algif_aead lets an unprivileged local user write four controlled bytes into the page cache of any readable file, leading to root. Actively exploited per CISA KEV. Affects 4.14 through 6.19.11 with stable-branch fixes at 5.10.254, 5.15.204, 6.1.170, 6.6.137, 6.12.85, 6.18.22, 6.19.12.
checks.remediation: Update the kernel to the relevant patched stable point. On Android: take the latest vendor OTA. On Linux distros: 'apt full-upgrade' / 'dnf update' / 'pacman -Syu' then reboot.
checks.why: AEAD interface allows tampering with cached file pages, including setuid binaries and credential stores.
checks.risk_if_fail: Local root via /etc/passwd or /usr/bin/su page-cache corruption.

checks.label: DirtyDecrypt (CVE-2026-31635) rxrpc rxgk page-cache write
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null); maj=$(echo "$v" | awk -F"[.-]" "{print \$1+0}"); min=$(echo "$v" | awk -F"[.-]" "{print \$2+0}"); rxrpc_loaded=$(grep -c "^rxrpc " /proc/modules 2>/dev/null || echo 0); rxrpc_proto=$(grep -c "^RxRPC" /proc/net/protocols 2>/dev/null || echo 0); if [ "$maj" -lt 6 ] || { [ "$maj" -eq 6 ] && [ "$min" -lt 16 ]; }; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED kernel $v rxgk introduced in 6.16"; elif [ "$rxrpc_loaded" = "0" ] && [ "$rxrpc_proto" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED rxrpc not active on $v"; else rxgk_cfg=""; if [ -r /proc/config.gz ]; then rxgk_cfg=$(zcat /proc/config.gz 2>/dev/null | grep "^CONFIG_RXGK="); fi; [ -z "$rxgk_cfg" ] && [ -r /boot/config-$v ] && rxgk_cfg=$(grep "^CONFIG_RXGK=" /boot/config-$v 2>/dev/null); if [ -z "$rxgk_cfg" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v rxrpc active CONFIG_RXGK unknown (kernel config not readable)"; else case "$rxgk_cfg" in *=y|*=m) echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v rxgk active $rxgk_cfg" ;; *) echo "NOT_AFFECTED kernel $v CONFIG_RXGK not enabled" ;; esac; fi; fi'
checks.description: Linux kernel net/rxrpc rxgk_decrypt_skb is missing the COW guard, allowing in-place decrypt to corrupt the page cache when frag pages come from splice. Only kernels with rxgk (6.16 and later) are affected, and only when rxrpc is loaded or built in AND CONFIG_RXGK is enabled. On Android (where /proc/config.gz and /boot/config-$(uname -r) are usually not readable), the check falls back to flagging when rxrpc is active and reports CONFIG_RXGK as unknown.
checks.remediation: Update to the rxrpc-fixed point release (commits a2567217ade9, beee051f259a, e2f1a80d8b1e). If rxrpc is not needed, blacklist it: 'echo install rxrpc /bin/false > /etc/modprobe.d/rxrpc.conf && rmmod rxrpc'.
checks.why: Same page-cache write primitive as Dirty Pipe, reached via the AFS RxRPC RESPONSE path.
checks.risk_if_fail: Local root via writing to setuid binaries or credential files in the page cache.

checks.label: Dirty Frag and Fragnesia (CVE-2026-43284, 43500, 46300) xfrm/ESP/RxRPC surface
checks.command: sh -c 'loaded=""; for m in esp4 esp6 rxrpc; do grep -q "^${m} " /proc/modules 2>/dev/null && loaded="${loaded} ${m}"; done; xfrm_active=$([ -e /proc/net/xfrm_stat ] && echo yes || echo no); esp_proto=$(awk "/^(ESP|esp)/" /proc/net/protocols 2>/dev/null | head -1 | awk "{print \$1}"); rxrpc_proto=$(awk "/^RxRPC/" /proc/net/protocols 2>/dev/null | head -1 | awk "{print \$1}"); mitig=""; for f in /etc/modprobe.d/dirtyfrag.conf /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist-dirtyfrag.conf; do [ -f "$f" ] && grep -qE "install (esp4|esp6|rxrpc) /bin/false" "$f" 2>/dev/null && mitig="${mitig} ${f}"; done; surface=0; [ -n "$loaded" ] && surface=1; [ "$xfrm_active" = "yes" ] && surface=1; [ -n "$esp_proto" ] && surface=1; [ -n "$rxrpc_proto" ] && surface=1; if [ "$surface" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED no xfrm/esp/rxrpc surface"; elif [ -n "$mitig" ]; then echo "MITIGATED loaded:${loaded:- none} blacklist:${mitig}"; else echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE loaded:${loaded:- none} xfrm:${xfrm_active} esp_proto:${esp_proto:-none} rxrpc_proto:${rxrpc_proto:-none}"; fi'
checks.description: Dirty Frag (xfrm-ESP and rxrpc page-cache write, CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500) and Fragnesia (xfrm ESP-in-TCP, CVE-2026-46300) all share the same attack surface: the xfrm/IPsec ESP code path and rxrpc, reachable via splice into the kernel page cache. Detection looks at both loadable modules and built-in surface (some Android kernels compile esp4/esp6 into the kernel), plus the standard blacklist mitigation file recommended by the V12 and V4bel PoCs.
checks.remediation: Apply the upstream patches that landed on 13 May 2026. If patching is delayed, drop the mitigation file: 'printf %s\\n "install esp4 /bin/false" "install esp6 /bin/false" "install rxrpc /bin/false" > /etc/modprobe.d/dirtyfrag.conf && rmmod esp4 esp6 rxrpc 2>/dev/null && echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches'. Breaks IPsec VPN and AFS until patched.
checks.why: Page-cache write primitive in a widely shipped subsystem, exploitable from an unprivileged local user namespace.
checks.risk_if_fail: Local root via in-page-cache overwrite of /usr/bin/su or /etc/shadow.

checks.label: Unprivileged user namespaces hardening (Fragnesia exploit precondition)
checks.command: sh -c 'mx=$(cat /proc/sys/user/max_user_namespaces 2>/dev/null); u=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone 2>/dev/null); aaur=$(cat /proc/sys/kernel/apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns 2>/dev/null); se=$(getenforce 2>/dev/null || cat /sys/fs/selinux/enforce 2>/dev/null); hardened=0; [ "$u" = "0" ] && hardened=1; [ "$aaur" = "1" ] && hardened=1; [ "$mx" = "0" ] && hardened=1; case "$se" in Enforcing|1) hardened=1 ;; esac; if [ "$hardened" = "1" ]; then echo "HARDENED max_userns=${mx:-na} userns_clone=${u:-na} apparmor=${aaur:-na} selinux=${se:-na}"; else echo "OPEN max_userns=${mx:-na} userns_clone=${u:-na} apparmor=${aaur:-na} selinux=${se:-na}"; fi'
checks.description: Most recent Linux LPE chains in this family (Fragnesia, Dirty Frag, Dirty Pipe variants) require the attacker to obtain CAP_NET_ADMIN inside an unprivileged user namespace via unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER). A hardened system either disables user namespaces (max_user_namespaces=0 or kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0), restricts them via AppArmor (Ubuntu 23.10+), or enforces SELinux (Android default and several Linux distros). Any one of those four mechanisms blocks the precondition.
checks.remediation: On Linux distros: 'sysctl -w kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0' or 'sysctl -w user.max_user_namespaces=0'. On Ubuntu 23.10 and later: keep 'kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1' (default). On Android: keep SELinux Enforcing.
checks.why: Defence in depth: removes the standard local-attacker entry point used by almost every recent kernel LPE PoC.
checks.risk_if_fail: Attacker has the namespace primitive needed to reach the vulnerable kernel paths.

checks.label: Keyring UAF (CVE-2016-0728) kernel < 4.4.1
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null); maj=$(echo "$v" | awk -F"[.-]" "{print \$1+0}"); min=$(echo "$v" | awk -F"[.-]" "{print \$2+0}"); pat=$(echo "$v" | awk -F"[.-]" "{print \$3+0}"); if [ "$maj" -lt 4 ] || { [ "$maj" -eq 4 ] && [ "$min" -lt 4 ]; } || { [ "$maj" -eq 4 ] && [ "$min" -eq 4 ] && [ "$pat" -lt 1 ]; }; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED kernel $v"; fi'
checks.description: Linux kernel join_session_keyring() reference-count error allowing local privilege escalation via crafted keyctl commands. Affects kernels older than 4.4.1. Old but still appears on long-tail IoT devices.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to 4.4.1 or later. If kernel cannot be updated, restrict access to keyctl(2).

checks.label: Qualcomm TrustZone privesc (CVE-2016-2431) Nexus 5/6/7/AndroidOne
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); board=$(getprop ro.product.board 2>/dev/null); soc=$(getprop ro.hardware 2>/dev/null); qcom=0; case "${board}${soc}" in *msm*|*qcom*|*sdm*|*sm[0-9]*|*MSM*) qcom=1 ;; esac; if [ "$qcom" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED non-qcom board=${board:-?} soc=${soc:-?}"; elif [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN qcom board, no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20160501" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE qcom patch=$sp pre-2016-05-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED qcom patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Qualcomm TrustZone component allowed crafted app to gain privileges on Nexus 5, 6, 7 (2013), and Android One devices on Android up to 6.0.1. Patched in Android Security Bulletin 2016-05-01.
checks.remediation: Install the 2016-05-01 or later Android security patch level.

checks.label: Qualcomm wcnss_wlan heap overflow (CVE-2016-5342)
checks.command: sh -c 'wcnss=$([ -e /dev/wcnss_wlan ] && echo present || echo absent); sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ "$wcnss" = "absent" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED no /dev/wcnss_wlan"; elif [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN wcnss present, no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20160701" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE /dev/wcnss_wlan present, patch=$sp pre-2016-07"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED /dev/wcnss_wlan present, patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Heap buffer overflow in Qualcomm wcnss_wlan_write writing unexpected sizes to /dev/wcnss_wlan. Affects kernel 3.x and Android up to 7.0. Local privilege escalation. Patched in Android Security Bulletin 2016-07-01.
checks.remediation: Install 2016-07-01 or later Android security patch level.

checks.label: qtaguid_untag UAF (CVE-2021-0399)
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20210301" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE patch=$sp pre-2021-03-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Use-after-free in qtaguid_untag in xt_qtaguid.c (netfilter quota tagging) on Android. Local privilege escalation. Patched in Android Security Bulletin 2021-03-01.
checks.remediation: Install 2021-03-01 or later Android security patch level.

checks.label: Binder UAF (CVE-2023-20938) binder_transaction_buffer_release
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20230201" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE patch=$sp pre-2023-02-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Use-after-free in binder_transaction_buffer_release in drivers/android/binder.c. Local privilege escalation, no user interaction. Patched in Android Security Bulletin 2023-02-01.
checks.remediation: Install 2023-02-01 or later Android security patch level.

checks.label: POSIX CPU timer race (CVE-2025-38352, actively exploited)
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F"[.-]" "{printf \"%d.%d.%d\", \$1, \$2, \$3}"); ka=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f1); kb=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f2); kc=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f3); vuln=0; case "${ka}.${kb}" in 2.6|3.*|4.*) vuln=1 ;; 5.4)  [ "$kc" -lt 295 ] && vuln=1 ;; 5.10) [ "$kc" -lt 239 ] && vuln=1 ;; 5.15) [ "$kc" -lt 186 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.1)  [ "$kc" -lt 142 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.6)  [ "$kc" -lt 94 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.12) [ "$kc" -lt 34 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.15) [ "$kc" -lt 3 ]   && vuln=1 ;; 5.*|6.*) vuln=1 ;; esac; [ "$vuln" = "1" ] && echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v" || echo "LIKELY_PATCHED kernel $v"'
checks.description: Race condition in posix-cpu-timers between handle_posix_cpu_timers and posix_cpu_timer_del. Local privilege escalation, in-the-wild exploitation since September 2025. Fixed in stable branches 5.4.295, 5.10.239, 5.15.186, 6.1.142, 6.6.94, 6.12.34, 6.15.3.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to the relevant fix point or take the latest Android vendor OTA.

checks.label: Qualcomm firmware memory corruption (CVE-2026-21385, CISA KEV)
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); vsp=$(getprop ro.vendor.build.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); board=$(getprop ro.product.board 2>/dev/null); soc=$(getprop ro.hardware 2>/dev/null); qcom=0; case "${board}${soc}" in *msm*|*qcom*|*sdm*|*sm[0-9]*|*MSM*) qcom=1 ;; esac; if [ "$qcom" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED non-qcom board=${board:-?} soc=${soc:-?}"; exit 0; fi; best=$sp; [ -n "$vsp" ] && [ "$vsp" -gt "${best:-0}" ] 2>/dev/null && best=$vsp; if [ -z "$best" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN qcom board, no security_patch property"; elif [ "$best" -lt "20260301" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE qcom patch=$best pre-2026-03-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED qcom patch=$best"; fi'
checks.description: Integer overflow / wraparound in Qualcomm firmware memory alignment leading to memory corruption. Actively exploited per CISA KEV (March 2026). Affects Snapdragon, FastConnect, modem and RF firmware. Patched in March 2026 vendor / Android bulletin.
checks.remediation: Take the March 2026 vendor OTA. Compare ro.vendor.build.security_patch to confirm the Qualcomm fix landed.

checks.label: rust_binder OOB write (CVE-2026-23194)
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F"[.-]" "{printf \"%d.%d.%d\", \$1, \$2, \$3}"); ka=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f1); kb=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f2); kc=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f3); vuln=0; case "${ka}.${kb}" in 6.18) [ "$kc" -lt 10 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.19) vuln=1 ;; esac; [ "$vuln" = "1" ] && echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v" || echo "NOT_AFFECTED kernel $v"'
checks.description: Out-of-bounds 8-byte write in rust_binder when handling empty FDA objects (skip==0 used as both a length and a pointer-fixup indicator). Affects kernel 6.18 pre-6.18.10 and 6.19-rc series. Local privilege escalation.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to 6.18.10 or later. Rust binder is a recent kernel feature, so older kernels are not affected.

checks.label: Android Security Bulletin compliance against known-exploited kernel CVEs
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN no ro.build.version.security_patch"; exit 0; fi; gap=""; chk() { d=$1; cve=$2; [ "$sp" -lt "$d" ] && gap="${gap} ${cve}(${d})"; }; chk 20160501 CVE-2016-2431; chk 20160701 CVE-2016-5342; chk 20161101 CVE-2016-5195; chk 20191001 CVE-2019-2215; chk 20200301 CVE-2020-0041; chk 20210301 CVE-2021-0399; chk 20211101 CVE-2021-1048; chk 20220401 CVE-2022-0847; chk 20230201 CVE-2023-20938; chk 20250901 CVE-2025-38352; chk 20260301 CVE-2026-21385; chk 20240501 CVE-2024-1086; chk 20240601 CVE-2024-32896; chk 20240801 CVE-2024-36971; chk 20241001 CVE-2024-43047; if [ -z "$gap" ]; then echo "COMPLIANT patch=$sp all listed exploited-CVE bulletins applied"; else echo "BEHIND patch=$sp missing:${gap}"; fi'
checks.description: Roll-up of the security patch level against the fix dates of the known-exploited CVEs tracked in this category. Every CVE it lists also has its own dedicated check, most of which additionally gate on the affected hardware and can therefore return NOT_AFFECTED where this roll-up cannot. It is reported at verify level so that it summarises rather than adding one more critical finding on top of the individual ones: an outdated device would otherwise raise this plus every CVE check behind it for the same underlying fact.
checks.remediation: Read this as an index. Act on the individual CVE checks, which carry the per-CVE hardware gating and remediation.

checks.label: netfilter nf_tables UAF (CVE-2024-1086, CISA KEV)
checks.command: sh -c 'v=$(uname -r 2>/dev/null | awk -F"[.-]" "{printf \"%d.%d.%d\", \$1, \$2, \$3}"); ka=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f1); kb=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f2); kc=$(echo "$v" | cut -d. -f3); vuln=0; case "${ka}.${kb}" in 3.*|4.*) vuln=1 ;; 5.0|5.1|5.2|5.3|5.4|5.5|5.6|5.7|5.8|5.9|5.10|5.11|5.12|5.13|5.14) vuln=1 ;; 5.15) [ "$kc" -lt 149 ] && vuln=1 ;; 6.0) vuln=1 ;; 6.1)  [ "$kc" -lt 76 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.2|6.3|6.4|6.5) vuln=1 ;; 6.6)  [ "$kc" -lt 15 ]  && vuln=1 ;; 6.7)  [ "$kc" -lt 3 ]   && vuln=1 ;; esac; nft_loaded=$(grep -c "^nf_tables " /proc/modules 2>/dev/null || echo 0); if [ "$vuln" = "1" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE kernel $v nf_tables_loaded=$nft_loaded"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED kernel $v"; fi'
checks.description: Use-after-free in nft_verdict_init in net/netfilter/nf_tables_api.c. Positive verdict values are treated as drop errors, causing double-free in nf_hook_slow. Public exploit code on GitHub. CISA KEV May 2024. Affects kernel 3.15 through 6.7.2 across all stable branches.
checks.remediation: Update to kernel 5.15.149+, 6.1.76+, 6.6.15+, or 6.7.3+. If patching is delayed, blacklist nf_tables via modprobe.d (will break netfilter rules that depend on nftables).

checks.label: Pixel logic-error privesc (CVE-2024-32896, CISA KEV)
checks.command: sh -c 'mfg=$(getprop ro.product.manufacturer 2>/dev/null); brand=$(getprop ro.product.brand 2>/dev/null); model=$(getprop ro.product.model 2>/dev/null); sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); pixel=0; case "${mfg}${brand}${model}" in *[Gg]oogle*|*[Pp]ixel*) pixel=1 ;; esac; if [ "$pixel" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED non-Pixel mfg=${mfg:-?} model=${model:-?}"; elif [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN pixel device, no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20240601" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE pixel patch=$sp pre-2024-06-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED pixel patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Logic error allowing local privilege escalation on Pixel devices. Actively exploited in-the-wild per CISA KEV (July 2024). Patched in June 2024 Pixel Update.
checks.remediation: Install the June 2024 (or later) Pixel security patch level.

checks.label: __dst_negative_advice UAF (CVE-2024-36971, CISA KEV)
checks.description: Race condition in __dst_negative_advice() failing to enforce RCU rules when clearing socket destination cache. Use-after-free in net/. Pixel zero-day, actively exploited in-the-wild per CISA KEV (August 2024). Affects 4.6 through patched points 4.19.317, 5.4.279, 5.10.220, 5.15.162, 6.1.95, 6.6.35, 6.9.5.
checks.remediation: Update kernel to the relevant patched stable point or take the latest Android OTA. Affected over a large range of Linux versions.

checks.label: Qualcomm DSP/FastRPC UAF (CVE-2024-43047, CISA KEV)
checks.command: N=$(ls -d /dev/adsprpc-smd /dev/cdsprpc-smd /dev/fastrpc* 2>/dev/null | sort -u | tr '\n' ' '); R=$([ -n "$N" ] && echo REACHABLE || echo NO_NODE); V=$(sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); vsp=$(getprop ro.vendor.build.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); board=$(getprop ro.product.board 2>/dev/null); soc=$(getprop ro.hardware 2>/dev/null); qcom=0; case "${board}${soc}" in *msm*|*qcom*|*sdm*|*sm[0-9]*|*MSM*) qcom=1 ;; esac; if [ "$qcom" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED non-qcom board=${board:-?} soc=${soc:-?}"; exit 0; fi; best=$sp; [ -n "$vsp" ] && [ "$vsp" -gt "${best:-0}" ] 2>/dev/null && best=$vsp; if [ -z "$best" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN qcom, no security_patch property"; elif [ "$best" -lt "20241001" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE qcom patch=$best pre-2024-10-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED qcom patch=$best"; fi'); printf '%s node=%s %s\n' "$V" "$R" "${N:-none}"
checks.description: Use-after-free in Qualcomm FastRPC / DSP service while maintaining memory maps of HLOS memory. Spyware-chain zero-day, actively exploited per CISA KEV (October 2024). Affects Snapdragon 8 Gen 1/2/3, FastConnect 6700/6800/6900/7800, automotive SA/SG, audio WCD. Patched in Qualcomm October 2024 security bulletin. This check now also probes whether the FastRPC device nodes are actually present, and reports node=REACHABLE or node=NO_NODE alongside the patch verdict. Previously it evaluated only the security patch date and the board string, so it could not distinguish a Qualcomm device where the vulnerable driver is exposed to apps from one where it is not present at all. The companion KDRV-FASTRPC-001 check reports the node permissions in full.
checks.remediation: Install the 2024-10-01 or later vendor security patch level. Compare ro.vendor.build.security_patch (or ro.build.version.security_patch on devices without separate vendor SPL).

checks.label: LANDFALL spyware chain (CVE-2025-21042 / CVE-2025-21043, CISA KEV) - Samsung
checks.command: sh -c 'mfg=$(getprop ro.product.manufacturer 2>/dev/null); brand=$(getprop ro.product.brand 2>/dev/null); sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); sam=0; case "${mfg}${brand}" in *[Ss]amsung*) sam=1 ;; esac; if [ "$sam" = "0" ]; then echo "NOT_AFFECTED non-Samsung mfg=${mfg:-?}"; elif [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN Samsung device, no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20250401" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE samsung patch=$sp pre-2025-04-01 (CVE-2025-21042 unpatched)"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20250901" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE samsung patch=$sp pre-2025-09-01 (CVE-2025-21043 unpatched)"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED samsung patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Out-of-bounds write vulnerabilities in the Samsung image codec library libimagecodec.quram.so, exploited zero-click via malicious DNG images (delivered over WhatsApp) to deploy the commercial-grade LANDFALL Android spyware against Samsung Galaxy devices. Campaign active since mid-2024, uncovered by Unit 42, added to CISA KEV in November 2025. CVE-2025-21042 was patched in the Samsung April 2025 SMR; the related CVE-2025-21043 was patched in September 2025. A Samsung device is only fully clear of the chain at security patch level 2025-09-01 or later. Non-Samsung devices report NOT_AFFECTED.
checks.remediation: Install the Samsung September 2025 security maintenance release (patch level 2025-09-01) or later. On managed Samsung fleets, treat any device below this SPL as high priority, this chain has been used in targeted, zero-click spyware attacks.

checks.label: Android Framework zero-day pair (CVE-2025-48633 / CVE-2025-48572, exploited)
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20251201" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE patch=$sp pre-2025-12-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Two Android Framework flaws flagged for limited, targeted in-the-wild exploitation in the December 2025 Android Security Bulletin: CVE-2025-48633 (High, information disclosure) and CVE-2025-48572 (High, local elevation of privilege). Both affect Android 13, 14, 15 and 16. Patched at security patch level 2025-12-01.
checks.remediation: Install the 2025-12-01 or later Android security patch level.

checks.label: Framework remote privesc, zero-interaction (CVE-2025-48595, exploited)
checks.command: sh -c 'sp=$(getprop ro.build.version.security_patch 2>/dev/null | tr -d -); if [ -z "$sp" ]; then echo "UNKNOWN no security_patch"; elif [ "$sp" -lt "20260601" ]; then echo "POTENTIALLY_VULNERABLE patch=$sp pre-2026-06-01"; else echo "LIKELY_PATCHED patch=$sp"; fi'
checks.description: Critical Android Framework vulnerability highlighted in the June 2026 Android Security Bulletin, enabling remote privilege escalation with no user interaction (no link click, app install, or other action required). Affects Android 14, 15, 16 and 16 QPR2. Patched at security patch level 2026-06-01.
